issue.title: Heap-use-after-free issue in `pyexpat` related to `.ExternalEntityParserCreate`

labels.name: type-bug
labels.description: An unexpected behavior, bug, or error

issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

When configured with `--with-address-sanitizer`, the test below crashes all versions of CPython:

```python
# Copyright (c) 2025 Sebastian Pipping <sebastian@pipping.org>
# Licensed under Zero-Clause BSD ("0BSD")

import pyexpat as expat
import unittest


class ParentParserLifetimeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """
    Subparsers make use of their parent XML_Parser inside of Expat.
    As a result, parent parsers need to outlive subparsers.
    Regression test for issue 139400
    """
    def test_parent_parser_outlives_its_subparsers(self):
        parser = expat.ParserCreate()
        subparser = parser.ExternalEntityParserCreate(None)

        # Now try to cause garbage collection of the parent parser
        # while it's still being referenced by a related subparser
        del parser


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
```

The finding was first documented at https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/139367#issuecomment-3343919109 .

comments.body: Out of curiosity, does it crash before Expat 2.7.2? I tried with on my Windows machine (no dev session) with Python 3.12.10, and there is no crash. It might be also related to some NDEBUG flag as I'm on a release build but I can't investigate more (or there might be a "silent" heap UAF). The Expat version being used is 2.7.1 there.
@picnixz does it have ASan baked in? I'm trying with latest CPython 3.9 (commit 4dea0fb67b7064eb637d859de0b5d3ce4989bd1c) now. It's Expat 2.7.1 there.

> [@picnixz](https://github.com/picnixz) does it have ASan baked in? I'm trying with latest CPython 3.9 (commit [4dea0fb](https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/4dea0fb67b7064eb637d859de0b5d3ce4989bd1c)) now. It's Expat 2.7.1 there.

Result: not affected.

@picnixz I'll try 3.13 with a revert to Expat 2.7.2 next, then with a revert to Expat 2.7.1. That should clarify involvement of Expat (although 3.14 with 2.7.3 _not_ being affected already pointed towards "not involved" — but let's see).

> does it have ASan baked in?

No, and that's why I'd like to know if it's an ASAN-only issue or not. Because IIRC, the failing CI tests weren't just affecting the ASAN build; it was affecting the regular builds (e.g., https://github.com/python/cpython/actions/runs/18046453659/job/51358293507?pr=139367)

> No, and that's why I'd like to know if it's an ASAN-only issue or not.

The tests [were all green for me before pushing the 3.13 pull request](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/139367#issuecomment-3339672239), so that means that with my local GCC the issue did not show prior to activating AddressSanatizer. _Could_ be the same for you.



> [@picnixz](https://github.com/picnixz) I'll try 3.13 with a revert to Expat 2.7.2 next, then with a revert to Expat 2.7.1. That should clarify involvement of Expat (although 3.14 with 2.7.3 _not_ being affected already pointed towards "not involved" — but let's see).

Update for 3.13: Same crash (as with 2.7.3) after reverting to 2.7.**2**, _no_ crash after reverting to 2.7.**1**. That's not expected and not good 😞

Tomorrow I'll (locally) try the following:

- Revert `pyexpat.c` in `main` to its state in `3.13`. This will revert the UB fixes and small other stuff but not by much (IOW, I'll just C/C the content of 3.13 to my local main).
- I'll try to see if I also have the failures *without ASAN* locally. Can you check with `clang` maybe? 

Aside from that, should I understand that it's possible that Expat 2.7.2 introduced a regression *but only* for 3.13 and below?
I marked the issues as blocked by this one (well, it could be other way around as well), but note that this should only be "blocking" for the backported branches prior to 3.14.

> Tomorrow I'll (locally) try the following:
> 
> * Revert `pyexpat.c` in `main` to its state in `3.13`.

I did this ⬆️ but with 3.14 (rather than `main`) just now (via `git checkout upstream-readonly/3.13 ./Modules/pyexpat.c`): _no_ crashes (and latest Expat 2.7.*3*).

Also also ran upstream Expat tests with `-O3` (as done in CPython) plus ASan: No crashes there.

@picnixz the reason 3.13 is crashing is because its `pyexpat` is freeing the parent Expat parser _while_ its subparser (created via `.ExternalEntityParserCreate`) is still referencing that parent (and using it even during its own freeing process since Expat >=2.7.2, which made this _appear_ as related earlier). Freeing the parent before its subparsers has never been safe use of Expat 😃 CPython 3.14 was lucky in my early tests but is also affected: _all_ versions of CPython are. So Expat is part if the symptom but not the cause. Phew! 😅 

I have created a pull request with a candidate fix now at #139403. It was exciting to work on and I'm looking forward to your review! 🙏
@picnixz PS: Could you re-label this issue to be about all versions of CPython, not just 3.13, for me? 🙏
No indeed it's not blocking anymore, though we can't backport the exposed Expat API to older branches due to the tests showing the crash, so I would prefer to still mark the latter as blocked.
@picnixz good point, so 1 blocked rather than 3 now, nice 👍
Actually, this one is independent of Expat so we can also fix Python 3.9 if we make it on time. If not, then unlucky 3.9 but it would at least be easier to fix than backporting all the new expat API.
Mmh. The question now is: do we want to backport this to 3.9 or not? I think so because the fix is not that huge and there is no "new" API here, right?
@picnixz 3.9 backport done (#139614). I should note that the 3.9 code in `xmlparse_traverse` does not visit `self`/`op`. I have not retro-added it so far.

> I should note that the 3.9 code in xmlparse_traverse does not visit self/op

Oh. I missed that part. Wait.

EDIT: it is fine not to visit the type because it's a static type. In 3.10+, the type is a heap type and we need to visit it.
